mainTopic: Prayers after תפילה, favorite sayings of the חכמים, and farewell blessings from the ישיבה
overview: The גמרא finishes a list, begun on the previous daf, of private prayers that חכמים added after their תפילה. We hear the end of רב ספרא's prayer for peace, then the prayers of רבי אלכסנדרי (with a dispute over which prayer was his), רבא (also used as רב המנונא זוטי's יום כפור confession), and מר בריה דרבינא, whose prayer is our אלהי נצור. רב ששת adds a fast-day prayer asking that the fat and blood he lost count as a קרבן. Next, the גמרא gathers sayings for other times. These include רבי יוחנן's words on finishing ספר איוב and the favorite sayings of רבי מאיר, the רבנן of יבנה, אביי, רבא, and רב. A side story tells how רבן יוחנן בן זכאי always greeted everyone first. The גמרא then teaches that women received a greater promise than men, and explains that they earn it by supporting their children's and husbands' Torah learning. It ends with the farewell blessings the חכמים gave each other when leaving the ישיבה, and a מחלוקת over the meaning of ״אלופינו מסבלים״.

steps.title: End of רב ספרא's prayer for peace among angels, חכמים, and students
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא's prayer ends by asking for peace among the heavenly group, the earthly group, and all Torah students, and that those who learn שלא לשמה should come to learn לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: …in the heavenly group and in the earthly group, and among the students who study Your Torah, whether they study it for its own sake or not for its own sake. And may it be Your will that all those who study not for its own sake will come to study for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The text picks up in the middle of רב ספרא's prayer from the previous daf, where he asks ה׳ to make peace. Here we hear the end of that prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ספרא asks for peace in three places: among the angels above, among the חכמים below, and among Torah students. He prays for all students, even those who learn for the wrong reasons. He also asks that those students grow into learning לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: An entourage or group that serves together
For its own sake, with pure motives

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a positive attitude toward learning שלא לשמה: such students are included in the prayer, with the hope that they will grow into learning לשמה.

phrases.english: in the heavenly entourage,
phrases.notes: We are joining רב ספרא's prayer midway. On the previous daf he began by asking ה׳ to make peace.

phrases.english: and in the earthly entourage,
and among the students who are busy with Your Torah,
whether they study it for its own sake
or study it not for its own sake.
And all those who study not for its own sake,
may it be Your will that they will study for its own sake."

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפָמַלְיָא שֶׁל מַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב ספרא's prayer, which began on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ספרא prayed for peace above and below, and for all Torah students, including that those learning שלא לשמה come to learn לשמה.

steps.title: רבי אלכסנדרי's prayer for a place of light
steps.stepSummary: After his תפילה, רבי אלכסנדרי asked to be placed in a corner of light and not darkness, and that his heart and eyes not grow weak.
steps.simpleTranslation: After his prayer, רבי אלכסנדרי said this: "May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that You place us in a corner of light and not in a corner of darkness, and that our hearts not become sick and our eyes not grow dim."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the next example in the list: the prayer רבי אלכסנדרי said after his תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a short prayer built on the contrast between light and darkness. He asks to be in a good, bright situation and not a dark one. He also asks to be spared sadness of the heart and dimness of the eyes.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אָלֶכְּסַנְדְרִי בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי:
phrases.english: רבי אלכסנדרי, after his prayer, said this:
"May it be Your will, ה׳ our God,
that You place us in a corner of light,
and do not place us in a corner of darkness,
and let our heart not become faint,
and let our eyes not grow dim."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אָלֶכְּסַנְדְרִי בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next sage's prayer in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלכסנדרי prayed to be placed in light and not in darkness, and to be spared weakness of heart and eyes.

steps.title: Another version: רבי אלכסנדרי's prayer about what holds us back
steps.stepSummary: Some say the light-and-darkness prayer was really רב המנונא's. In this version, רבי אלכסנדרי's prayer was: we want to do Your will, but the yeast in the dough and the rule of foreign kingdoms stop us, so save us from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that the prayer above is the one רב המנונא used to say, and that רבי אלכסנדרי, after he prayed, said this: "Master of the worlds, it is clear and known before You that we want to do Your will. So what holds us back? The yeast in the dough and being enslaved to the kingdoms. May it be Your will that You save us from their hands, so that we can go back to doing the laws You want with a whole heart."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of who said what. In this version, the light-and-darkness prayer belongs to רב המנונא, and רבי אלכסנדרי said a different prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase איכא דאמרי brings a different report of the same tradition. רבי אלכסנדרי's prayer says that deep down we really want to serve ה׳. Two things block us: the יצר הרע inside us (the 'yeast in the dough') and the pressure of foreign rulers from outside.

keyTerms.meaning: The yeast in the dough, meaning the יצר הרע

steps.confusionAlert: The איכא דאמרי does not drop the first prayer. It only moves it to רב המנונא and gives רבי אלכסנדרי a different prayer.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous expression of the idea that a Jew's true inner will is to do ה׳'s will, and that sin comes from outside forces holding him back.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, הָא רַב הַמְנוּנָא מְצַלֵּי לַהּ.
phrases.english: Some say: that one, רב המנונא used to pray it.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the light-and-darkness prayer we just learned.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אָלֶכְּסַנְדְרִי בָּתַר דִּמְצַלֵּי אָמַר הָכִי:
phrases.english: And רבי אלכסנדרי, after he prayed, said this:
"Master of the worlds, it is clear and known before You
that our will is to do Your will.
And who holds us back?
The yeast in the dough, and enslavement to the kingdoms.
phrases.notes: The 'yeast in the dough' is the יצר הרע. Like yeast, it works from inside and puffs a person up.

phrases.english: May it be Your will that You save us from their hands,

phrases.aramaic: וְנָשׁוּב לַעֲשׂוֹת חוּקֵּי רְצוֹנְךָ בְּלֵבָב שָׁלֵם״.
phrases.english: and we will return to doing the laws of Your will with a whole heart."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, הָא רַב הַמְנוּנָא מְצַלֵּי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of who said the prayer in step 2, and adds a different prayer for רבי אלכסנדרי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, רב המנונא said the light prayer. רבי אלכסנדרי prayed to be saved from the יצר הרע and foreign rule so he could serve ה׳ wholeheartedly.

steps.title: רבא's humble prayer for forgiveness without suffering
steps.stepSummary: רבא admits his own lowliness, asks never to sin again, and asks that his past sins be wiped away through mercy, not through suffering and illness.
steps.simpleTranslation: After his prayer, רבא said this: "My God, before I was formed I was not worthy, and now that I have been formed it is as if I was not formed. I am dust while I live, and all the more so when I die. Here I am before You like a vessel full of shame and embarrassment. May it be Your will, ה׳ my God, that I not sin again. And what I have already sinned before You, wipe it clean in Your great mercy, but not through suffering and bad illnesses."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the next sage's prayer, the one רבא said after his תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא first humbles himself. Before birth he did not count, and even now he has not become worthy. He uses a קל וחומר: if I am dust now, I will surely be dust after death. Then he asks for two things: not to sin anymore, and to have old sins cleaned away gently through mercy, not through pain.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so; reasoning from a lesser case to a greater one

phrases.english: רבא, after his prayer, said this:
"My God, before I was formed I was not worthy,
and now that I have been formed, it is as if I was not formed.

phrases.aramaic: עָפָר אֲנִי בְּחַיַּי, קַל וָחוֹמֶר בְּמִיתָתִי,
phrases.english: I am dust in my life, all the more so in my death.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אֲנִי לְפָנֶיךָ כִּכְלִי מָלֵא בּוּשָׁה וּכְלִימָּה.
phrases.english: Here I am before You like a vessel full of shame and embarrassment.

phrases.aramaic: יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהַי, שֶׁלֹּא אֶחֱטָא עוֹד,
phrases.english: May it be Your will, ה׳ my God, that I will not sin again,
and what I have sinned before You,
wipe clean in Your great mercy,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא עַל יְדֵי יִסּוּרִין וָחֳלָאִים רָעִים״.
phrases.english: but not through sufferings and bad illnesses."

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main list with the next sage's prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא prayed with deep humility to sin no more and to have his past sins cleansed through mercy, not suffering.

steps.title: רבא's prayer is רב המנונא זוטי's יום כפור confession
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this same prayer of רבא is the וידוי that רב המנונא זוטי said on יום כפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the confession of רב המנונא זוטי on יום כפור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short note to the prayer it just quoted: these same words were used as a יום כפור confession.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It points out that רבא's words served a second role, as רב המנונא זוטי's וידוי. That makes sense, since the prayer is full of admitting lowliness and asking that sins be wiped away.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same as

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why the words עד שלא נוצרתי appear in the יום כפור וידוי to this day.

phrases.english: And this is the confession of רב המנונא זוטי
on יום כפור.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ וִידּוּי דְרַב הַמְנוּנָא זוּטֵי בְּיוֹמָא דְכִפּוּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies רבא's prayer from step 4 with a known יום כפור confession.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא's prayer is the same text that רב המנונא זוטי used as his יום כפור וידוי.

steps.title: מר בריה דרבינא's prayer: אלהי נצור
steps.stepSummary: When מר בריה דרבינא finished his תפילה, he asked ה׳ to guard his speech, keep him humble and silent before insults, open his heart to Torah, protect him from harm, and stop those plotting against him. He ended with יהיו לרצון.
steps.simpleTranslation: When מר the son of רבינא finished his prayer, he said this: "My God, guard my tongue from evil and my lips from speaking deceit. To those who curse me, let my soul be silent, and let my soul be like dust to everyone. Open my heart to Your Torah, and let my soul run after Your מצוות. Save me from a bad mishap, from the יצר הרע, from a bad woman, and from all evils that rush to come into the world. And all who plan evil against me, quickly break their plans and spoil their thoughts. May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be pleasing before You, ה׳, my Rock and my Redeemer."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the next prayer in this list, the one מר בריה דרבינא said at the end of his תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prayer moves in order. First he asks for control of speech and humility before others. Then he asks to grow in Torah and מצוות, and then for protection from outside and inside dangers and from enemies' plots. He closes with the פסוק יהיו לרצון, asking that all his words be accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: A bad mishap or harmful encounter
That rush in, that suddenly come

steps.whatToRemember: מר בריה דרבינא's prayer is the source of אלהי נצור. Many חכמים added a personal request after their תפילה, each reflecting their own concerns: peace, light, freedom to serve ה׳, forgiveness, and guarding one's speech. The next step adds one more such prayer, from רב ששת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This prayer is the source of אלהי נצור, which is said at the end of every שמונה עשרה.

phrases.english: מר the son of רבינא,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה מְסַיֵּים צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי:
phrases.english: when he would finish his prayer, said this:
"My God, guard my tongue from evil
and my lips from speaking deceit.
And to those who curse me, may my soul be silent,
and may my soul be like dust to everyone.
Open my heart to Your Torah,
and may my soul chase after Your commandments.
And save me from a bad mishap, from the evil inclination,
and from a bad woman,
and from all evils that rush to come into the world.
And all who plan evil against me,
quickly break their plan and spoil their thoughts.

phrases.aramaic: יִהְיוּ לְרָצוֹן אִמְרֵי פִי וְהֶגְיוֹן לִבִּי לְפָנֶיךָ
phrases.english: May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be pleasing before You,
ה׳, my Rock and my Redeemer."

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא כִּי הֲוָה מְסַיֵּים צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next sage's prayer in the same list of prayers said after תפילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מר בריה דרבינא ended his תפילה by asking to guard his speech, stay humble, grow in Torah, be protected from harm, and have his words accepted.

steps.title: רב ששת's prayer that his fasting count as a sacrifice
steps.stepSummary: After praying on a fast day, רב ששת asked ה׳ to accept the fat and blood he lost through fasting as if he had offered them as a קרבן on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב ששת was fasting, after his תפילה he said: Master of the world, You know that when the בית המקדש stood, a person who sinned brought a קרבן. Only its fat and blood were offered, and he was forgiven. Now I have fasted, and my own fat and blood have become less. May it be Your will that this loss count as if I offered it to You on the מזבח, and may You accept me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more prayer said after תפילה, this time by רב ששת on a fast day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת makes a comparison. In a קרבן, the parts placed on the מזבח were the fat and blood, and that brought forgiveness. Fasting makes a person's own fat and blood smaller, so he asks that this loss count like a קרבן today, when there is no בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: A sacrifice offered in the בית המקדש
Its fat and its blood, the parts of the animal placed on the מזבח
And may You accept me favorably

steps.whyThisMatters: This prayer gives a well-known idea: when there is no בית המקדש, a person's fasting and the loss it causes can stand in place of a קרבן.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת כִּי הֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּתַעֲנִיתָא,
phrases.english: When Rav Sheshet would sit in a fast,
after he prayed, he would say this:
"Master of the worlds, it is known before You
that when the Beis HaMikdash is standing,
a person sins and brings a korban.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַקְרִיבִין מִמֶּנּוּ, אֶלָּא חֶלְבּוֹ וְדָמוֹ,
phrases.english: And they offer from it only its fat and its blood,
and he is forgiven.
And now I have sat in a fast,
and my fat and blood have become less.
May it be Your will
that my fat and blood that became less

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִילּוּ הִקְרַבְתִּיו לְפָנֶיךָ עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: be as if I offered it before You on the altar,
and may You accept me favorably."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת כִּי הֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּתַעֲנִיתָא, בָּתַר דִּמְצַלֵּי אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of prayers said after תפילה (following מר בריה דרבינא), now a special prayer for a fast day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fasting, which reduces a person's fat and blood, can be offered to ה׳ in prayer as if it were a קרבן on the מזבח.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's words after finishing ספר איוב
steps.stepSummary: When רבי יוחנן finished learning ספר איוב, he said that every living thing dies, so happy is the one who lives with Torah, pleases his Creator, and leaves the world with a good name, as שלמה said in קהלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוחנן finished ספר איוב, he said: In the end a person dies and an animal is slaughtered. Everyone is headed toward death. Happy is the one who grew up in Torah and worked hard in Torah, who brings joy to his Creator, who grew up with a good name and left the world with a good name. About him שלמה said: A good name is better than good oil, and the day of death is better than the day of birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves from prayers after תפילה to sayings the חכמים said at other times, starting with what רבי יוחנן said when he finished ספר איוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ספר איוב is full of suffering and death, so רבי יוחנן reminds us that death comes to everyone. What really matters is how a person lived: with Torah, pleasing ה׳, and keeping a good name until the end. The פסוק from קהלת shows that for such a person, the day he dies is better than the day he was born.

keyTerms.meaning: His hard work is in Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new group in the sugya: sayings for special times, not only prayers after תפילה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כִּי הֲוָה מְסַיֵּים סִפְרָא דְאִיּוֹב,
phrases.english: When Rabbi Yochanan would finish the book of Iyov,
he would say this: "In the end a person will die,
and in the end an animal will be slaughtered,
and all of them are headed toward death.

phrases.aramaic: אַשְׁרֵי מִי שֶׁגָּדֵל בַּתּוֹרָה וַעֲמָלוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Happy is the one who grew up in Torah and whose hard work is in Torah,
who brings pleasure to his Creator,
who grew up with a good name
and left the world with a good name.
And about him Shlomo said:
'A good name is better than good oil,'
'and the day of death than the day of one's birth.'"

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כִּי הֲוָה מְסַיֵּים סִפְרָא דְאִיּוֹב, אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from prayers said after תפילה to sayings said at other times, here at the end of learning ספר איוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since everyone dies, a person's true success is a life of Torah, pleasing ה׳, and keeping a good name until the end.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's favorite saying about learning Torah and fearing God
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר often repeated a saying in ה׳'s voice: learn My ways with all your heart, guard My Torah, fear Me, keep your mouth and self pure, and I will be with you everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר often said: Learn with all your heart and soul to know My ways, and stay at the doors of My Torah. Keep My Torah in your heart, and keep fear of Me before your eyes. Guard your mouth from every sin, and make yourself pure and holy from all wrongdoing. Then I will be with you everywhere.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the saying that רבי מאיר liked to repeat often, spoken as if ה׳ is talking to the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying lists what ה׳ asks: learn Torah with full effort, keep it in your heart, fear ה׳, and keep your speech and self clean from sin. At the end comes a promise: if you do this, ה׳ will be with you wherever you are.

keyTerms.meaning: A saying he often repeated (literally: a pearl in his mouth)
To be diligent, to keep coming back

phrases.english: A saying Rabbi Meir often repeated:
phrases.notes: Literally 'a pearl in the mouth of רבי מאיר', meaning a favorite saying he always had ready.

phrases.english: "Learn with all your heart and with all your soul
to know My ways,
and to be diligent at the doors of My Torah.
Keep My Torah in your heart,
and fear of Me should be before your eyes.
Guard your mouth from every sin,

phrases.aramaic: וְטַהֵר וְקַדֵּשׁ עַצְמְךָ מִכָּל אַשְׁמָה וְעָוֹן.
phrases.english: and purify and sanctify yourself from all guilt and sin.
And I will be with you in every place."

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the collection of favorite sayings of the חכמים, now from רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who learns Torah fully, fears ה׳, and keeps himself pure from sin will have ה׳ with him everywhere.

steps.title: The רבנן of יבנה: the Torah scholar and the worker are equal before God
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן of יבנה often said that a Torah scholar and a field worker are both ה׳'s creations, each doing his own work. Neither should look down on the other, because what matters is not how much one does but that his heart is directed לשמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן of יבנה often said: I am a creation of ה׳, and my friend is a creation of ה׳. My work is in the city, and his work is in the field. I get up early for my work, and he gets up early for his work. Just as he does not try to take over my work, I do not try to take over his work. And if you say: I do a lot of Torah and he does only a little, we already learned: whether one does a lot or a little, it is the same, as long as he directs his heart לשמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the favorite saying of the רבנן of יבנה, which teaches a Torah scholar not to feel better than a person who works in the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholar first says both of them are ה׳'s creations, each working hard at his own job. Then he raises a possible objection himself: I learn much more Torah than he does. He answers with a known teaching that doing much or doing little counts the same, as long as the heart is directed לשמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Tries to take over, or claims for himself
The one who does a lot and the one who does a little
That he directs his heart toward Heaven

steps.whatToRemember: In this group of sayings the חכמים keep returning to the heart: fasting as a קרבן, a life of Torah and a good name, fear of ה׳, and directing the heart לשמים. What counts most is a person's intention, not how much he does.
steps.confusionAlert: The question 'perhaps you will say, I do a lot and he does a little' is not the גמרא challenging anyone. It is part of the רבנן's own saying. They raise the thought themselves so they can reject it.

phrases.english: A saying the Rabbis of Yavne often repeated:
"I am a creation, and my friend is a creation.
My work is in the city,
and his work is in the field.
I get up early for my work,
and he gets up early for his work.
Just as he does not try to take over my work,
so I do not try to take over his work.

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר: אֲנִי מַרְבֶּה, וְהוּא מַמְעִיט —
phrases.english: And perhaps you will say: I do a lot, and he does a little,
phrases.notes: He means: I learn a lot of Torah, and he learns only a little, so I must be better.

phrases.english: we have learned: whether one does a lot or one does a little,
it is the same, as long as he directs his heart toward Heaven."

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמַּיְיהוּ דְּרַבָּנַן דְּיַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of favorite sayings (after רבי מאיר), now from the רבנן of יבנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Torah scholar must not feel better than a working person. Doing a lot or a little is equal, as long as one's heart is directed לשמים.

steps.title: אביי: Be clever in fear of Heaven and increase peace with everyone
steps.stepSummary: אביי often said that a person should use clever strategies to grow in יראת שמים. He should give soft answers and build peace with everyone, even a non-Jew in the market, so that he is loved by ה׳ and by people.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי used to say: A person should always be clever in how he serves ה׳. As the פסוק says, 'A soft answer turns away anger.' He should increase peace with his brothers, his relatives, every person, and even a non-Jew in the market. That way he will be loved above, liked below, and accepted by everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another favorite saying, this time from אביי, about using smart and gentle behavior to serve ה׳ and to make peace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ערום usually means 'sly,' but here אביי uses it in a positive way: be smart in finding ways to serve ה׳. His main tool is a soft answer that calms anger, which builds peace with everyone. The reward reaches two places at once: being loved by ה׳ and being liked by people.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular saying in his mouth, something he often said
Clever in fear of Heaven, using smart strategies to serve ה׳

phrases.english: A regular saying in the mouth of אביי was:
A person should always be clever in fear of Heaven.
"A soft answer turns away anger."

phrases.aramaic: וּמַרְבֶּה שָׁלוֹם עִם אֶחָיו וְעִם קְרוֹבָיו
phrases.english: And he should increase peace with his brothers and with his relatives

phrases.aramaic: וְעִם כָּל אָדָם וַאֲפִילּוּ עִם גּוֹי בַּשּׁוּק,
phrases.english: and with every person, even with a non-Jew in the market,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא אָהוּב לְמַעְלָה וְנֶחְמָד לְמַטָּה,
phrases.english: so that he will be loved above and pleasant below,
and he will be accepted by people.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of favorite sayings of the חכמים, following the saying of the רבנן of יבנה in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Use clever, gentle strategies to grow in יראת שמים, and build peace with all people so that you are loved by ה׳ and by people.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי always greeted others first
steps.stepSummary: As a side note, the גמרא reports that nobody ever greeted רבן יוחנן בן זכאי first, not even a non-Jew in the market, because he always greeted them first.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי that no one ever greeted him before he greeted them, not even a non-Jew in the market.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short story about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי that shows אביי's teaching about peace in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said to increase peace 'even with a non-Jew in the market.' רבן יוחנן בן זכאי lived exactly this way: he was always the first to say שלום to anyone. The repeated words 'גוי בשוק' tie the story to אביי's saying.

keyTerms.meaning: Greeted him first, said שלום before he did
A non-Jew in the market, a stranger with no connection to him

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: They said about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
that no person ever greeted him first,
not even a non-Jew in the market.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side story that shows אביי's teaching about peace, even with a non-Jew in the market, being lived out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי always greeted every person first, even a stranger in the market.

steps.title: רבא: The goal of wisdom is repentance and good deeds, done for their own sake
steps.stepSummary: רבא often said that the purpose of Torah wisdom is תשובה and good deeds. Learning should never make a person arrogant toward his parents, his רבי, or greater people. He proves from a פסוק that only those who act לשמה gain real understanding, and says that one who acts שלא לשמה would be better off not created.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא used to say: The goal of wisdom is תשובה and good deeds. A person should not learn Torah and then kick at his father, mother, רבי, or someone greater than him in wisdom or in number. As it says: 'The beginning of wisdom is fear of ה׳, good understanding to all who do them.' It doesn't say 'to those who do' but 'to those who do them,' meaning those who do it לשמה, not those who do it שלא לשמה. Anyone who does it שלא לשמה, it would be better for him not to have been created.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's favorite saying: Torah learning must lead to תשובה, good deeds, and humility, and it must be done לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא warns against a person who learns but becomes arrogant and disrespects his parents and teachers. He reads the extra word 'them' in עושיהם as limiting the reward to those who do it the right way, לשמה. He ends with a sharp line: doing it שלא לשמה is so bad that not being created would be better.

keyTerms.meaning: The goal or purpose of wisdom
For its own sake, for the right reason
It would be better for him not to have been created

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבא says one who acts שלא לשמה would be better off not created, yet elsewhere the גמרא encourages learning even שלא לשמה because it leads to לשמה. רבא's warning here is aimed at someone who learns in order to become arrogant and disrespect others, as his opening words describe.

phrases.english: A regular saying in the mouth of רבא was:
The goal of wisdom is repentance and good deeds,
so that a person should not read and learn
and then kick at his father, his mother, and his teacher

phrases.aramaic: וּבְמִי שֶׁהוּא גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ בְּחָכְמָה וּבְמִנְיָן,
phrases.english: and at someone who is greater than him in wisdom and in number,
as it is said: "The beginning of wisdom is fear of ה׳,
good understanding to all who do them."
It does not say "to those who do," but "to those who do them":
to those who do it for its own sake,
and not to those who do it not for its own sake.
And anyone who does it not for its own sake,
it would be better for him had he not been created.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the list of favorite sayings after the side story about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah wisdom must lead to תשובה, good deeds, and humility, and must be done לשמה; one who does it שלא לשמה would be better off not created.

steps.title: רב: The World to Come is not like this world
steps.stepSummary: רב often said that עולם הבא is completely different from this world. There is no eating, drinking, having children, business, jealousy, hatred, or competition. Instead צדיקים sit with crowns on their heads and enjoy the glow of the שכינה, as the פסוק about seeing ה׳ shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב used to say: עולם הבא is not like this world. In עולם הבא there is no eating, no drinking, no having children, no business, no jealousy, no hatred, and no competition. Instead, צדיקים sit with their crowns on their heads and enjoy the glow of the שכינה, as it says: 'They saw God, and they ate and drank.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב's favorite saying, which describes what עולם הבא is like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב first removes everything physical from עולם הבא, including bodily needs, business, and the bad feelings that come from competing. What remains is pure closeness to ה׳: the צדיקים enjoying the שכינה. The פסוק shows that seeing ה׳ was itself like eating and drinking for them, so that is the 'food' of עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The glow or splendor of ה׳'s Presence

steps.whatToRemember: This section of the גמרא gathers favorite sayings of the Sages. אביי stresses peace with everyone, רבא stresses humble learning לשמה, and רב teaches that the real reward in עולם הבא is closeness to the שכינה, not physical pleasure.

phrases.english: A regular saying in the mouth of רב was:
The World to Come is not like this world.

phrases.aramaic: הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא אֵין בּוֹ לֹא אֲכִילָה וְלֹא שְׁתִיָּהּ
phrases.english: In the World to Come there is no eating and no drinking,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה וְלֹא מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן
phrases.english: no having children and no business dealings,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא קִנְאָה וְלֹא שִׂנְאָה וְלֹא תַּחֲרוּת,
phrases.english: no jealousy, no hatred, and no competition,
but rather the righteous sit with their crowns on their heads
and enjoy the glow of the Divine Presence,
as it is said: "And they saw God,
and they ate and drank."

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another favorite saying in the same list, moving from how to live in this world to what awaits in עולם הבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולם הבא has no physical activity or rivalry; צדיקים sit with crowns and enjoy the glow of the שכינה.

steps.title: Women received a greater promise than men
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that ה׳ promised women more than men, and brings a פסוק from ישעיהו as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: The promise that ה׳ made to women is greater than the one He made to men. The פסוק says: 'Women who are at ease, rise up and hear My voice; daughters who are confident, listen to My words.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another short saying about reward: women were given a bigger promise than men. It proves this from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls women 'at ease' (שאננות) and 'confident' (בוטחות). The גמרא reads these words as a promise of calm and security that is not said this way about men.

phrases.aramaic: גְּדוֹלָה הַבְטָחָה שֶׁהִבְטִיחָן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: Great is the promise that the Holy One, Blessed be He, promised them
to women, more than to men,
as it says: 'Women at ease, rise up,
hear My voice;
confident daughters, listen to My words.'

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּדוֹלָה הַבְטָחָה שֶׁהִבְטִיחָן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְנָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of sayings about reward, after רב's description of עולם הבא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳'s promise to women is greater than His promise to men, as shown by the words 'at ease' and 'confident' in the פסוק.

steps.title: רב asks how women earn this reward
steps.stepSummary: רב asks רבי חייא what women do to earn such a great reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to רבי חייא: Through what do women earn this reward?
steps.whatsHappening: רב asks a question about the saying we just learned. He wants to know what women do to deserve this reward, and the next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes that reward comes from doing מצוות and learning Torah. Since women are not obligated in תלמוד תורה the way men are, רב wants to know where their great reward comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: They earn merit, they deserve reward

phrases.english: Rav said to Rabbi Ḥiyya:
Women, through what do they earn merit?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא: נָשִׁים בְּמַאי זָכְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the promise to women in the previous step
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do women do that earns them this great promise?

steps.title: Women earn it by supporting Torah learning
steps.stepSummary: Women earn merit by bringing their children to learn, sending their husbands to learn, and waiting for them to come home.
steps.simpleTranslation: By bringing their children to learn reading in the בית כנסת, by sending their husbands to learn in the בית מדרש, and by waiting for their husbands until they come back from the בית מדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the answer to רב's question. Women earn their reward by making it possible for their children and husbands to learn Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer lists three things: taking children to learn, sending husbands to learn, and waiting patiently for them to return. The point is that helping others learn Torah earns a share in that Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: The בית כנסת, where children were taught to read
The house of the חכמים, the study hall

steps.whatToRemember: Women earn their great reward by supporting the Torah learning of their children and husbands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that someone who makes it possible for others to learn Torah shares in the reward of that learning.

phrases.english: By bringing their sons to learn reading in the synagogue,
and by sending their husbands to learn in the study hall,
and by waiting for their husbands
until they come back from the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאַקְרוֹיֵי בְּנַיְיהוּ לְבֵי כְנִישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב's question from the previous step
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Women earn merit by bringing children to learn, sending husbands to learn, and waiting for them to return.

steps.title: The farewell blessing at the ישיבה of רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: When the חכמים left the ישיבה of רבי אמי (or רבי חנינא), they gave each other a long blessing for this world, עולם הבא, and success in Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the חכמים left the ישיבה of רבי אמי (some say רבי חנינא), they would bless each other like this: May you enjoy your world in your lifetime, may your end be life in עולם הבא, and may your hope last for many generations. May your heart think deeply, your mouth speak wisdom, and your tongue sing praise. May your eyes look straight ahead, shine with the light of Torah, and may your face glow like the sky. May your lips speak knowledge, your inner feelings rejoice in what is right, and your feet run to hear the words of ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now records the blessing the חכמים gave each other when they took leave of one another at the ישיבה to go home. It is a long blessing covering this world, עולם הבא, and growth in Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing starts with the whole person's life: this world, עולם הבא, and future generations. Then it goes body part by body part (heart, mouth, tongue, eyes, face, lips, kidneys, feet) and asks that each one be filled with Torah. It fits the earlier steps that connect Torah and good deeds with real reward.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Ancient of Days', a name for ה׳

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲווֹ מִפַּטְרִי רַבָּנַן מִבֵּי רַבִּי אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: When the Sages would take leave of the study hall of Rabbi Ami,
and some say, of the study hall of Rabbi Ḥanina,
they would say to him like this:
'May you see your world in your lifetime,
phrases.notes: He means: may you enjoy all the good of this world while you are alive.

phrases.english: and may your end be to life in the World-to-Come,
and may your hope last for many generations.
May your heart think about understanding,
your mouth speak wisdom,
and your tongue whisper songs of praise.
May your eyelids look straight ahead of you,
your eyes shine with the light of Torah,
and your face glow like the brightness of the sky.
May your lips express knowledge,
your kidneys rejoice in what is upright,
phrases.notes: In the language of תנ״ך, the kidneys stand for a person's deepest thoughts and feelings.

phrases.english: and your feet run to hear
the words of the Ancient of Days.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲווֹ מִפַּטְרִי רַבָּנַן מִבֵּי רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new related theme: blessings the חכמים gave when leaving a ישיבה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the חכמים parted from each other, they would bless one another with good in this world, life in עולם הבא, and Torah filling every part of his being.

steps.title: The farewell blessing at the ישיבה of רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: When the חכמים left the ישיבה of רב חסדא (or רבי שמואל בר נחמני), they blessed each other with a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the חכמים left the ישיבה of רב חסדא (some say רבי שמואל בר נחמני), they would say to each other the פסוק: 'Our leaders are loaded down...' and the rest of the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second farewell blessing, this time from a different ישיבה. Here the חכמים used a פסוק instead of a long blessing of their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא quotes only the start of the פסוק, 'Our leaders are loaded down,' and says 'etc.' This step only records that this was the blessing they used. The next step explains what the words mean.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Etc.', meaning continue with the rest of the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים had a custom of blessing each other when they parted at the ישיבה, sometimes with a long blessing and sometimes with a פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲווֹ מִפַּטְרִי רַבָּנַן מִבֵּי רַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: When the Sages would take leave of the study hall of Rav Ḥisda,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ מִבֵּי רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי,
phrases.english: and some say, of the study hall of Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani,
they would say to him like this:
'Our leaders are loaded down, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲווֹ מִפַּטְרִי רַבָּנַן מִבֵּי רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second example of a farewell blessing, parallel to the previous step
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At רב חסדא's ישיבה, the farewell blessing was the פסוק 'Our leaders are loaded down.'

steps.title: Two explanations of 'our leaders are laden'
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל (or רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר) argue about the meaning of ״אלופינו מסבלים״. One says it means leaders in תורה who carry many מצוות; the other says it means leaders in תורה and מצוות who carry יסורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Our leaders are laden": רב and שמואל, and some say רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר, explained it differently. One said: 'our leaders' in תורה are 'laden' with מצוות. The other said: 'our leaders' in תורה and מצוות are 'laden' with יסורים (suffering).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the first words of the פסוק from תהלים that the חכמים used as a blessing in the last step. Two אמוראים give two different explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that 'our leaders' means people who are great in תורה. They argue about what these leaders are 'laden' (loaded) with. The first says they carry many מצוות on top of their תורה; the second says they are great in both תורה and מצוות, and what they carry is suffering.

keyTerms.meaning: One said (one side of a dispute)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think there are four separate opinions here. There are only two opinions; the גמרא just isn't sure whether the pair arguing was רב and שמואל or רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: "Our leaders are laden":
phrases.notes: These are the opening words of the פסוק quoted in the last step, תהלים 144:14.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar, [disagreed]:
One said: "Our leaders" in Torah
are "laden" with מצוות.
And one said: "Our leaders" in Torah and מצוות
are "laden" with suffering.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר: ״אַלּוּפֵינוּ״ — בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the opening words of the פסוק from תהלים that was used as the blessing in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״אלופינו מסבלים״ refers to leaders in תורה; one view says they are laden with מצוות, the other says leaders in תורה and מצוות are laden with יסורים.
